audit.whatIsWrong: Eternal Hunger is described as keyed to YOUR health — 'heals more the lower your HP drops' (early), 'heals harder the lower he drops you' (whys[0]), 'his missing-HP passive' used for both halves of the same sentence.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Warwick's basic attacks deal bonus magic damage. If WARWICK is below 50% health, he heals the same amount. If WARWICK is below 25% health, this healing triples.' It is his missing health, not yours. That inversion changes the plan completely. As written, the page implies you can starve the heal by staying healthy; in reality the heal switches on precisely when you have chunked him, so a half-committed trade is the worst possible trade — you hand him the 50% threshold and then walk away. It also mis-sources the one thing that IS keyed to your health: Blood Hunt senses enemies below 50% and frenzies below 25%, which is the real reason 'never fall below half' is correct advice.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger heals HIM off HIS own missing health — on below 50%, tripled below 25%. Blood Hunt is the one that watches YOUR health.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl does not appear anywhere on the page — not in early, mid, late, any why-row, any spike, or the cooldowns block.
audit.why: It is 15/14/13/12/11 seconds and does two things that both land directly on Kassadin's plan: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second.' The damage reduction blanks a blink-in burst — the exact 2.5-second window the page tells you to commit into — and the fear at the end throws you out of your own combo while you are standing at 375 range with no escape but a 500-unit blink. A page whose whole level 6 instruction is 'blink in, E-Q-auto, blink out' cannot omit the button that turns that sequence off.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl (15s at rank 1) is 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that ends in a 1-second fear. Do not dump your burst into it, and expect to be feared out of the follow-up.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (E description, cooldown 15/14/13/12/11, range 375, hardCC flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress is named as the clock of the lane in six strings with no cooldown and no suppress duration, and Blood Hunt is treated as a permanent aura with no cooldown either.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 seconds with a 1.5-second suppression, and it leaps a distance that scales with his bonus move speed. Blood Hunt is 80/70/60/50/40 seconds at 4000 range and only activates against targets below 50% health. Those two numbers reshape the lane: at rank 1 his engage tool is on nearly two minutes, and his chase tool is on eighty seconds and conditional on you being hurt. 'Track it before every step-up' becomes a real schedule rather than a vibe.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress: 110s at rank 1, 1.5s suppress. Blood Hunt: 80s at rank 1, and it only switches on once you drop below half.

audit.why: Jaws of the Beast is correctly treated as sustain, and it is worth recording why the flagged 'resistances-invalidated' interaction does not need new text: Riot's description is 'dealing damage based on their maximum health', so armour and magic resist are the wrong purchase against it — and the page never recommends resistances into him anyway. Its 8s cooldown at rank 1 and 365 range are the numbers a reader would want, but the page's existing framing is not wrong, so I spent the budget on the two outright errors above.

Sides untouched. The shape holds even after the passive correction — Warwick owns 1-3 harder than the page realised (his sustain gets better as you chunk him), 4-5 is where Nether Blade stabilises you, 6 is Skill, and the item stages stay contested because Blood Hunt still closes on a hurt Kassadin. 63.16% over 19 games is a whole-game figure and the page's own late-game rows already carry that story.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late: 'Q-silence the counterplay'. Separately, the _missing-interactions file says Warwick can cancel your Null Sphere with Primal Howl or Infinite Duress — I did not write that in.
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels and shields against magic; it has never silenced. And the your-channel-punished flag is a false positive on Kassadin generally: it fires off a 'channel' derived flag that the kit builder attached to Null Sphere because its tooltip contains the words 'interrupting channels'. Null Sphere is a point-and-click orb with no channel to break.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence, and it is not a channel his CC can break.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q description and its derived 'channel' flag)

audit.why: 63.16% over 19 games. The page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Warwick, full stop. His Eternal Hunger passive heals more the lower your HP drops, and his Jaws of the Beast (Q) heal gives him sustain you can't match, so any trade you start where you step up to E him is one he wins back on-hit. You have only Null Sphere, no escape, and a mana pool that drains fast. Last-hit from the edge of your E cone, eat the poke, and never fall below half — that's where his missing-HP passive and Blood Hunt attack speed turn a poke into a kill.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Warwick, full stop. Eternal Hunger heals him off HIS own missing health — on below 50%, tripled below 25% — so chunking him halfway makes his sustain better, not worse, and Jaws of the Beast (8s) bites for max health and heals again on top. You have only Null Sphere, no escape, and a mana pool that drains fast. Last-hit from the edge of your E cone, and never fall below half yourself: that is the threshold that switches Blood Hunt on.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the stabilization that tips toward you: max Q for the shield and waveclear, lean on Nether Blade's (W) huge mana restore to stay topped up, and farm under tower while you track his cooldowns. Then Level 6 flips the lane outright — Riftwalk is your escape AND your engage. When he commits Blood Hunt to chase, blink out so he can't path to you, then R back in for an E-Q-auto trade with the Q shield eating his return damage. Bait Infinite Duress; once that suppress is on cooldown he has nothing to pin you with.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the stabilization that tips toward you: max Q for the shield and waveclear, lean on Nether Blade's mana restore to stay topped up, and farm under tower while you count his cooldowns. Then 6 flips the lane — Riftwalk is your escape AND your engage. Blood Hunt is 80s at rank 1 and only switches on below half health, so stay above it. Bait Infinite Duress (110s, a 1.5s suppress), then go — but never dump burst into Primal Howl's 2.5s of damage reduction, which ends in a fear.

notes: One thing I could not resolve from the files and did not write either way: Infinite Duress carries a 'channel' derived flag in Warwick's kit, and Kassadin's Null Sphere 'interrupts channels'. If that interrupt applies to Warwick's suppression, Kassadin has a counterplay to the single most feared ability in this matchup and the page should lead with it; if it only applies to the Katarina-style channelled ultimates, then writing it in would get people killed. Riot's text does not settle it and the kit file's needsResearch block is empty, so it is in questionsForUser. Also of note: three of the four Kassadin matchups I have audited so far claim Void Stone reduces magic damage by exactly 15%; Riot publishes no figure. I have left the number in place everywhere rather than swap one unsourced claim for another, but it wants a single decision applied repo-wide.
